name: CoolCAD Electronics Inc.
old_description: CoolCAD Electronics is an innovative company that designs and fabricates semiconductor devices and chips made from wide bandgap semiconductor Silicon Carbide (SiC).
about:
CoolCAD Electronics operates from Greenbelt, Maryland, where it designs and fabricates semiconductor devices and chips from wide-bandgap silicon carbide (SiC). The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm produces SiC MOSFETs, diodes, high-temperature integrated circuits, and deep-ultraviolet optical sensors. Its proprietary SiC formulations and manufacturing processes enable devices that operate continuously at temperatures exceeding 400 °C, well above the 200 °C limit of conventional silicon chips. CoolCAD also offers research and development services, computer-aided design and thermal simulation through its CoolSPICE software, cryogenic and radiation testing for space and nuclear applications, and engineering support for transitioning existing silicon-based power devices to SiC.

Customers span aerospace, automotive, data communications, green energy, military and defense, power generation, and water purification sectors. The company's high-temperature ICs and UV sensors are positioned for extreme-environment applications such as deep-space exploration, nuclear energy monitoring, and daylight UV imaging without optical filters.

CoolCAD holds multiple U.S. patents covering wide-bandgap SiC semiconductor advances. The technology was developed to accelerate the shift from fossil-fuel infrastructure toward renewable energy systems by delivering higher voltage, higher power, and smaller, lighter electronic systems.

name: Cooper Lighting (Eaton)
old_description: Manufactures LED lighting fixtures and controls (Cooper Lighting Solutions, part of Eaton).
about:
Cooper Lighting Solutions, a business unit of Signify, is headquartered in Peachtree City, Georgia. The company traces its roots to 1833 with the founding of Cooper Industries, which later became part of Eaton before being acquired by Signify in 2020.

The company manufactures LED lighting fixtures and controls across a portfolio of brands including HALO, PrentaLux, WaveLinx, Nemalux, Metalux, and Lumark. Its Americus, Georgia facility has earned NEMA Make It American certification, verifying domestic content compliance. The product range spans commercial downlights, high-bay luminaires, outdoor lighting, marine-grade fixtures, decorative luminaires, and wireless control systems such as WaveLinx with DMX integration. Manufacturing capabilities include pressure-equalization valve technology, 3D-printed decorative shades, and design-for-disassembly practices that avoid glue, paint, or potting.

Cooper Lighting Solutions serves commercial, industrial, marine, hospitality, multi-family, retail, and manufacturing sectors. Its products are specified by architects, engineers, and contractors for applications ranging from office and retail spaces to harsh marine environments and large-scale industrial facilities. The company also provides building-readiness tools for life-safety and egress lighting testing.

The company emphasizes sustainability and transparency: all PrentaLux products carry Declare labels disclosing material content above 100 ppm, and the firm targets net-zero emissions by 2040 through its parent Signify. Its "Closing the Loop" initiative enables product refreshment without full replacement, and the NEMA Make It American certification underscores a commitment to domestic manufacturing.

name: Copack Utah
old_description: Many formulas require much more than a good sanitary blender; they require a properly developed blending procedure that is customized to each formula.
about:
Based in Lindon, Utah, Copack Utah operates as a contract blending and packaging service for dry food products. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure.

Its core offering is custom dry blending, where each formula receives a tailored procedure that determines the number of blending stages, ingredient sequencing, and the choice between high-shear or gentle tumble action. Packaging capabilities cover automated pouch and bag lines (including stand-up, flat, custom-shaped, and side-gusset formats), canning lines for 603 x 701 (#10) cans, and bulk options such as tote bags, lined boxes, and pails. Nitrogen flushing is available for oxygen-sensitive products.

The service targets food manufacturers that need outsourced blending and packaging, though the company does not name specific industries or customers. Quality assurance rests on a HACCP-based food safety plan supplemented by independent laboratory testing for microbiological, allergen, water activity, and atmospheric parameters.

Copack Utah emphasizes flexibility, offering custom lot coding, special receiving requirements, and tailored shipping arrangements. Once a custom service is established, the company stresses dependability as a key differentiator.

name: CorVent Medical, Inc
old_description: Simple, Safe, and Smart critical care respiratory ventilation solutions designed to support hospitals, long-term care facilities, and government stockpiles.
about:
CorVent Medical, Inc. is based in Fargo, North Dakota, where it designs and manufactures critical care respiratory ventilation solutions. The company’s flagship product, the RESPOND® Ventilator, is developed and built in the United States to serve hospitals, long-term care facilities, government stockpiles, and rural health clinics. CorVent Medical emphasizes simplicity, safety, and smart technology to reduce complexity in critical care ventilation.

The RESPOND® Ventilator provides ICU-standard ventilation in a lightweight, portable platform. It supports invasive and non-invasive modes for patients from pediatrics (≥38 kg) through adults, with adjustable settings for flow triggering, oxygen concentration, and PEEP. Built-in safeguards include high inspiratory pressure, disconnect, and apnea alarms. The system operates with any low-flow oxygen source, uses multi-stage antiviral filters rated at 99.99% efficiency, and requires no proprietary circuits or high-pressure gas. A hot-swappable battery provides up to three hours of runtime, while nurse call ports and EMR connectivity enable remote monitoring and documentation. CorVent Medical backs the device with a five-year standard warranty and eliminates service and maintenance contracts.

The company serves acute care hospitals, critical access hospitals (CACs), long-term care hospitals (LTCHs), skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), and government stockpile managers. Its customer base includes respiratory therapy directors, chief nursing officers, ICU directors, and financial officers. CorVent Medical offers nationwide product demonstrations and evaluations to support procurement decisions.

CorVent Medical was founded to address the urgent need for reliable, efficient, and safe ventilation systems that lower total cost of ownership. The company holds ISO 13485 certification and complies with FDA 21 CFR 820.30 and current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP). Its differentiators include a five-year warranty without service contracts, no proprietary consumables, and independence from high-pressure oxygen infrastructure.

name: Corbeau
old_description: Our seats are the product of 60+ years of experience building and perfecting high-performance seating.
about:
Corbeau was founded in 1966 in Bluffdale, Utah, and has spent more than six decades developing high-performance seating. The company operates from a facility in the Salt Lake City area, where it designs and manufactures seats for street, race, off-road, gaming, and office applications.

The product line includes reclining and fixed-back racing seats, ergonomic office chairs, and a comprehensive range of custom brackets engineered for specific vehicle models. Corbeau emphasizes a perfect-fit approach, pairing each seat with a bracket built for the exact make and model, eliminating the guesswork of mixing components from different suppliers.

The company serves motorsport enthusiasts, automotive aftermarket customers, gamers, and office professionals worldwide. Its seats are marketed for street driving, track competition, off-road use, gaming setups, and workplace ergonomics, with examples such as the Trailcat, FX1 Pro, RRS, and A4 models.

Corbeau cites its 60-year legacy as its primary differentiator, claiming the industry's largest seat and bracket selection. It also highlights direct customer service—real-person phone support from its Utah facility, quick email replies, and a pledge that every shipped product meets or exceeds expectations.

name: Cord Apparel
old_description: Custom Clothing Manufacturers & Trusted Apparel Manufacturing Partner
about:
Cord Apparel operates from Missouri City, Texas, providing full-service apparel manufacturing for brands across the United States. The company does not disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders publicly. It was created to address inconsistency in the domestic clothing manufacturing market, offering a streamlined alternative to managing multiple vendors.

The company produces a range of garments including T-shirts, hoodies, activewear, denim, baby apparel, and leather goods. Its capabilities cover screen printing, sublimation, embroidery, custom packaging, cut-and-sew assembly, product development and sampling, fabric sourcing with quality control, and private-label branding. Cord Apparel handles both small-batch and bulk production runs, emphasizing low minimum-order quantities for startups and scalable systems for growing labels.

Clients include fashion startups, direct-to-consumer brands, scaling apparel labels, established fashion houses, and promotional product companies. The manufacturer positions itself as a USA-focused partner, highlighting clear timelines, accountability, and multi-stage quality inspections as key to its service.

Cord Apparel differentiates itself by focusing on people and products rather than volume, aiming to democratize high-end manufacturing for emerging brands. Its stated values include uncompromised quality, continuous innovation, sustainability, inclusive sizing, transparent communication, and ethical labor practices. A nine-step production roadmap — from discovery consultation through ongoing support — structures each project.

about:
Cornerstone Woodworking Co. operates from Neenah, Wisconsin, where owners Troy and Stacy Weyenberg lead a custom cabinetry and woodworking business. Troy Weyenberg, a master craftsman with nearly 30 years in home building and remodeling, oversees production, finishing, and installation. Stacy Weyenberg, a kitchen and bath designer with an interior design background, guides clients through space planning, cabinetry layouts, and finish selection.

The company produces custom cabinetry for residential and commercial projects, including kitchens, bathrooms, pantries, laundry rooms, mudrooms, entertainment centers, and home offices. Its in-house process covers design, production, finishing, and installation, with an emphasis on high-quality materials and craftsmanship. The shop also handles furniture making and millwork for a range of built-in and freestanding pieces.

Cornerstone serves homeowners, builders, interior designers, and general contractors across residential and commercial sectors. The team coordinates directly with other trades on job sites, ensuring that cabinetry integrates smoothly with plumbing, electrical, and structural work. Past projects span single-family remodels, new construction, and commercial fit-outs.

The Weyenbergs emphasize a collaborative, owner-managed approach: Troy supervises each project from the shop floor to final installation, while Stacy works closely with clients to translate functional needs into personalized designs. The company states that its differentiation lies in coordinating every stage—design, production, finishing, and installation—under one roof, maintaining direct communication with clients and trade partners throughout.

name: Corrugated Containers
old_description: For the best experience on our site, be sure to turn on Javascript in your browser.
about:
Corrugated Containers, Inc. operates from its corporate headquarters in Cayce, South Carolina, with a second branch in Duncan near the BMW manufacturing campus. The company traces its roots to the early 1970s when it began in a small warehouse in downtown Columbia. In the late 1970s the business moved to Cayce, where several warehouses have been added over the past two decades. A first branch opened in the Greenville‑Spartanburg area in 2001, and a new warehouse was built in Duncan in 2004. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The firm is a wholesale distributor of shipping supplies serving the southeastern United States. It stocks hundreds of box sizes — single‑wall, double‑wall, die‑cut, file, record‑storage, bin, 32 ECT and 44 ECT, and Gaylord containers — along with tape, stretch wrap, strapping, bubble wrap, kraft paper, and bubble‑lined envelopes. Overrun boxes, some with existing print, are offered at 25‑40 % off list price. The product line also includes packing‑list envelopes, poly bags, stretch film and dispensers, tape dispensers, and cushioning materials such as packing peanuts, newsprint, polyethylene foam, and CORROFLEX corrugated wrap.

Customers range from industrial manufacturers to e‑commerce shippers that need packages ready for UPS or common‑carrier pickup. The company’s own directory lists custom packaging for aerospace and automotive sectors, and its Southeast footprint supports regional distributors and OEMs alike.

Corrugated Containers emphasizes fast, dependable service at competitive prices, backed by a large in‑stock inventory and the ability to provide samples on request. The overrun program and multi‑location warehousing are cited as key advantages for buyers seeking quick turnaround on standard and specialty shipping containers.

name: Corvia Medical
old_description: CAUTION–Investigational Device. Limited by United States Law to Investigational Use.
about:
Corvia Medical is based in Tewksbury, Massachusetts. The company has been led since 2010 by President and CEO George Fazio, a veteran of the medical device industry with prior leadership roles at St. Jude Medical. The leadership team includes Chief Medical Officer Jan Komtebedde, Vice President of R&D and Operations Ed McNamara, and Vice President of Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs Kate Stohlman.

The company is focused on developing an investigational medical device aimed at transforming the standard of care for heart failure treatment. The device is currently limited to investigational use under United States law. Corvia Medical’s operations span research and development, clinical strategy, regulatory affairs, and quality assurance, with a team experienced in cardiovascular device development from prototype through commercialization.

Corvia Medical operates in the cardiovascular medical device sector, targeting heart failure treatment. Its investigational device is being evaluated through clinical trials, with the aim of serving interventional cardiologists and healthcare systems once approved.

The company was built on the collective experience of its leadership team, which brings decades of expertise in structural heart and interventional cardiology devices from companies such as St. Jude Medical, Abbott Vascular, and Medtronic. This background informs Corvia’s approach to developing novel therapies for heart failure.

name: Countryside Amish Furniture
about:
Countryside Amish Furniture operates from Arthur, Illinois, where owner Mel Stutzman purchased the business in 2010 after more than 25 years working in Amish furniture shops. Raised Amish with formal schooling ending at eighth grade, Stutzman progressed from sanding to finish room to shop foreman before moving into custom cabinetry. The company remains family-owned and operated, drawing on Stutzman’s direct experience to vet partner workshops.

The retailer offers made-to-order solid wood furniture across dining, office, bedroom, living room, nursery, and outdoor categories, with thousands of designs spanning Traditional, Farmhouse, Mission, Shaker, and Contemporary styles. Production is distributed among more than 100 family-run Amish workshops in Pennsylvania, Indiana, and Ohio. Customers select from North American hardwoods — oak, cherry, brown maple, tiger maple, walnut — and choose stains, fabrics, leathers, or Sunbrella outdoor textiles. Each piece is built with mortise-and-tenon, dovetail, and tongue-and-groove joinery, hand-sanded, and finished with catalyzed conversion varnish. Countryside coordinates the process, provides free material samples, and ships finished goods to the contiguous 48 states for a flat $150 fee that includes in-home placement and assembly.

The primary customer base is residential, though a dedicated trade program serves interior designers and commercial buyers. Orders are split with half due at the shop and half at finishing, and lead times typically run 14 to 18 weeks.

Stutzman’s hands-on background drives the quality standards: he inspects hidden surfaces, requires solid hardwood for structural components, and insists on cut joinery that accommodates seasonal wood movement. The sales team maintains high-touch communication throughout the build, updating clients until delivery.
